title: Cross-pod rapid embed: 9-day activation playcard
content:
Purpose:
Short, practical playcard to onboard and evaluate cross-pod embeds (internal transfers, short-term contractors, and rotational mentors) over a 9-day activation window. Aim: get person productive on a measurable slice of work, validate skill fit, and produce a binary decision signal (continue / extend / offboard).

Scope & intended users:
- Used by hiring managers, mentors, Eng managers, and people-ops coordinators.
- Best for embeds that need to land quickly into incident ops, small infra fixes, experiment wiring, or narrow feature ownership.

Quick summary timeline (9 days):
- Day 0 (pre-embed): access + context + 60m async brief sent
- Day 1–2: orientation, stakeholding, small shadow tasks
- Day 3–5: primary task workblock + daily mentor sync (15m)
- Day 6–7: integration & handoff polish; first draft deliverable produced
- Day 8: review, rubric scoring, risk/impact notes
- Day 9: debrief + decision (extend | convert | offboard) + retro notes

Pre-embed checklist (to complete 24–72h before start):
- Manager: confirm target deliverable (MVP scope <= 3h/day of focused work)
- Mentor: schedule 15–30m daily stand window and book 1h review on Day 8
- IT: invite to required Slack channels, grant GitHub repo read/write, assign access to infra staging project
- People Ops: calendar invite with expectations doc, payroll/contract setup if needed, UXR/Legal flags if customer data involved
- Share a 1-page context brief: problem statement, acceptance criteria, linked tickets, helpful PRs

Interview & selection rubric (for rotational candidates) — quick scoring (0–2 each):
- Task alignment (0: poor, 1: borderline, 2: good) — candidate shows direct experience with the domain
- Hands-on deliverable skill (0–2) — can prototype or debug in target stack within timebox
- Communication & async culture (0–2) — clear PRs, check-ins, notes to stakeholders
- Ownership hunger & escalation (0–2) — asks the right questions, raises risks early
- Team fit & coachability (0–2) — accepts feedback and pivots quickly
Pass threshold: 7/10 recommended to run the 9-day embed. 9–10: strong candidate for conversion.

Interview prompts (short, sharp):
- Give me a 20-minute plan to ship a minimal rollback-safe hotfix for a botched model route. What do you check first?
- Walk me through a recent engineering handoff you did. What did you document, what failed, and what would you change?
- Show a quick GitHub snippet or local repro that demonstrates your approach to debugging a latency spike.

Role-specific acceptance criteria (examples — manager should define 1–3 items):
- Example infra embed: produce a small canary deployment, validate telemetry, and document rollback steps
- Example feature embed: implement and test a single endpoint, wire the route, add smoke tests, and open PR with runbook
- Example eval embed: run a 1k-prompt smoke eval, summarize precision/recall/regressions, and create follow-up tickets

Daily mentor cadence template (15m):
- Yesterday (10–20m of async notes): what you did, open blockers (share link to PRs/tickets)
- Today (what will you try to finish? blockers?)
- Risk signal: green / yellow / red (one-line rationale)
Use this as a standing Slack thread or a tiny Google Doc that both can edit.

Deliverable hygiene & PR checklist:
- Small, focused PRs < 300 lines ideally
- Clear description + how to test locally + expected telemetry impact
- Automated tests where feasible, else smoke test steps included
- Runbook stub if the change touches prod-facing behavior

Day 8 review rubric (scoring + notes):
- Deliverable completeness (0–3): meets acceptance criteria, minor polish left, or incomplete
- Impact (0–3): low / medium / high risk and reward
- Code quality (0–2): maintainable, tested, documented
- Collaboration (0–2): clear handoff artifacts, knowledge share
Decision guidance:
- Score >=7 and mentor recommends: extend or convert to longer engagement (outline next tranche)
- Score 4–6: conditional extension + targeted development plan (2 week trial)
- Score <=3: offboard with clear feedback and knowledge capture

Risk register (common items + mitigations):
- Access delays: mitigation — start with a shadow/day-zero replicate environment and pair on screen share
- Scope creep: mitigation — freeze MVP scope on Day 1 and require managerial sign-off for new tasks
- Customer data exposure: mitigation — involve security lead in Day 0 access gating and use sanitized datasets
- Mentor bandwidth gap: mitigation — backup mentor designated (can be 30m/week) and async Q/A doc

Offer/extension script (people-ops template) — short email/Slack + follow-up call:
- Quick Slack: "We loved your work during the embed. Manager recommends extending to X weeks to complete [deliverable]. Can we discuss terms?"
- Follow-up email: include extension scope, proposed rate/comp, conversion timeline, and next steps for payroll/contractual changes

Metrics / success signals (to track across embeds):
- Time-to-first-merge (target <= 5 days)
- Deliverable acceptance rate (goal >= 75%)
- Conversion rate to longer engagement / perm hire (target 30% within cohort)
- Mentor satisfaction score (post-embed quick survey)

Templates to attach / copy: (placeholders below)
- One-page context brief (title, problem, tickets, acceptance criteria, helpful links)
- Mentor daily note template (single paragraph + risk color)
- Day 8 rubric form (checkbox + short comment fields)

Notes to self / open questions:
- Do we want a small stipend for mentors to account for extra synchronous load? (ops cost analysis needed)
- How to track payroll conversions cleanly in Workday — coordinate with People Systems
- Pilot this with 6 embeds in Q1; capture standardized metrics + 1 retrospective per cohort

Appendix: quick checklist (copyable)
- [ ] Context brief shared
- [ ] Accesses granted (Slack, GitHub, infra)
- [ ] Mentor calendar booked
- [ ] First-day 60m kickoff on calendar
- [ ] MVP acceptance criteria defined and agreed
- [ ] Day 8 review slot reserved
- [ ] Offboarding checklist drafted in case of negative decision

Endnotes:
This is intentionally lightweight — the emphasis is on a rapid, measurable trial with clear acceptance criteria. Keep the paperwork small and the evidence concrete.
